failure_modes.title: Parenthetical alias-of and coordinated-clause sub-element-of mention not extracted
failure_modes.symptom: L missed links when a subject-position multi-word-phrase is followed by a parenthetical containing coordinated-clause alternatives that function as alias-of or sub-element-of evidence for multiple targets. The sentence expresses storage/location with one head-noun in the main clause, while the parenthetical introduces two distinct candidate mentions; both were under-rejected.
failure_modes.apparent_cause: The current bank is empty, so there is no extraction rule that promotes parenthetical mentions into standalone candidates when they appear after an indefinite-article or qualifier-clause introducing a specific location/container. L appears to rely on exact-match in the main clause and does not propagate links from parenthetical coordinated-clause mentions.
failure_modes.suggested_direction: Add extraction rules that detect parenthetical coordinated-clause mentions after a location/container head-noun and emit separate candidates for each coordinated sub-element. Treat each parenthetical noun phrase as alias-of or sub-element-of the introduced location phrase, then allow propagated linking to multiple targets.
failure_modes.abstract_example_pair:
TP: "The records are kept in a dedicated location (e.g., a remote unit or a local unit) to separate the archive from the registry." -> extract links to both parenthetical mentions.
FP: "The records are kept in a dedicated location (for example, for reliability) near the registry." -> do not create entity links from a parenthetical that lacks noun-phrase candidates.

failure_modes.title: Contrastive sentence-initial marker suppresses downstream entity extraction
failure_modes.symptom: L missed valid links in a sentence whose sentence-position begins with a contrastive discourse marker and whose predicate describes where a subject-position phrase is stored. The contrastive opener appears to reduce confidence for otherwise valid mentions later in the sentence.
failure_modes.apparent_cause: Without judge rules for discourse markers, L may overweight local lexical continuity from the previous sentence and under-approve mentions in a sentence introduced by contrast. The bank lacks rules stating that contrastive sentence-position markers do not negate entity mentions in the same predicate.
failure_modes.suggested_direction: Add judge rules that preserve candidate validity under sentence-initial contrastive markers when the main predicate still asserts container-of or location relations. The rule should separate discourse function from mention validity.
failure_modes.abstract_example_pair:
TP: "By contrast, the attachments are placed in a separate repository." -> keep the repository mention valid.
FP: "By contrast, the previous assumption was incorrect." -> do not infer any entity link when no container-of predicate is present.

failure_modes.title: Multi-target propagation from one sentence not supported
failure_modes.symptom: A single sentence supports more than one target through coordinated-clause or parenthetical alternatives, but L validated none of them. This indicates missing propagated approval from one discourse unit to multiple sub-elements.
failure_modes.apparent_cause: Current validation likely assumes one dominant target per sentence or requires a single exact-match anchor. With no validation rules in the bank, there is no mechanism to approve multiple links when a sentence explicitly enumerates alternatives under one container/location phrase.
failure_modes.suggested_direction: Add validation rules allowing one sentence to support multiple links when coordinated noun phrases appear inside a parenthetical or apposition attached to the same head-noun. Validate each sub-element independently if the predicate applies to the whole coordinated structure.
failure_modes.abstract_example_pair:
TP: "The snapshots are written to a backup area (a primary node or a secondary node)." -> validate links to both nodes.
FP: "The snapshots are written to a backup area, or discarded." -> do not validate two targets when the coordination is at predicate level rather than noun-phrase level.
